# Grok Bot skills, plugins, and MCP servers

> Curated directory of skills, plugins, MCP servers and self-hosted alternatives for Grok Bot, the always-on AI teammate from xAI/SpaceXAI and Cursor, each with its own persistent cloud computer. Includes the primary-source read on how Grok Bot is actually extended.

This repository has one curated surface and four generated ones. `README.md` is written by hand and
is where entries are added; `CATALOG.md`, `catalog.csv`, `plugins.json` and `EVENTS.md` are rebuilt
from live sources and are never edited by hand. Prefer a generated file when you want fields; prefer
the README when you want the reasoning.

## Files

- [README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-grok-bot/main/README.md): the curated list. Headings cover what Grok Bot is and how it is actually extended, pricing and access, a comparison against OpenClaw and Hermes Agent, events and community, the catalog itself, and cross-references to adjacent lists. Entries are markdown bullets under H3 headings, each carrying the entry name, its repository link, the author, a one line description and a stability tag.
- [CATALOG.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-grok-bot/main/CATALOG.md): every entry as one table row, with stars, licence, skill count and which manifest formats it actually ships.
- [catalog.csv](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-grok-bot/main/catalog.csv): the same set as CSV, one row per entry, with the manifest columns split out per client plus the open Agent Plugins schema flag.
- [plugins.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-grok-bot/main/plugins.json): the same set as JSON, with a top level `count` and `updated` date.
- [EVENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-grok-bot/main/EVENTS.md): every upcoming Grok Bot meetup, workshop and hackathon, with the organiser's local time and the UTC equivalent, rebuilt from each registration page. Events that have started are deleted rather than kept.
- [badges/](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-grok-bot/main/badges/entries.json): shields.io endpoint payloads for the entry count, the `.grok-plugin` share and the last-checked timestamp. The counts rendered on the README come from these, so no number on the page is typed by hand.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-grok-bot/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): the bar an entry has to clear and the exact format a new entry uses.

## What is checked here, and what is not

- Grok Bot launched in beta and its extension surface is not what most write-ups assume. The
  mechanisms described in the README are each checked against xAI's own documentation or a real
  install, and the section says which. Prefer that section over any recalled assumption about how
  Grok Bot loads third-party code.
- Every linked repository is re-resolved through the GitHub API weekly, which catches the renames,
  archives and deletions that a plain HTTP check passes clean because all three still return 200.
  Links are swept for rot on the same cadence.
- Which manifest formats an entry ships is read from that repository's own file tree, never inferred
  from its name or its description. A tree that could not be read is reported as "Not established"
  and counted apart from both buckets, never as "no manifest found".
- Marketplace entries are resolved at the exact commit xAI's marketplace pins, not at the source
  repository's HEAD, because the pinned commit is what actually gets loaded.
- No entry carries a per-entry verification mark in this repository. Presence in the list means the
  entry resolved and was read against a primary source at its last pass, nothing stronger.
- This is a curated list, not a security review. Anything installed here runs with the permissions
  of whoever installed it.

## How an agent should use this list

1. Fetch `catalog.csv` or `plugins.json` for fields, or `README.md` for the descriptions and the
   reasoning. Each is complete on its own; the counts in all of them come from the same run.
2. Before answering "how do I extend Grok Bot", read the extension-mechanism section. It is the part
   most often got wrong from memory.
3. Take install and configuration commands verbatim from the fenced block beside the entry.
4. Quote the entry's own description and link to its source. Do not invent authors, licences,
   pricing or install commands that are not in the file. Pricing and beta status change; treat both
   as of the date shown next to them.
5. Ask the person before installing anything or handing it credentials.
6. To add or correct an entry, open a pull request against this repository. There is no write API
   and nothing here accepts a direct push.
